nodes.content: Predict yeast growth effects of unseen mutation combinations across genetic backgrounds while distinguishing transferable epistasis from background-specific interactions.
requirements: Reduce combination-level RMSE by 10% versus background-aware additive models on unseen genetic backgrounds.
Exceed 75% accuracy identifying epistasis sign changes across backgrounds for independently measurable nonadditive effects.

nodes.content: Fit a pathway-regularized hierarchical growth model separating transferable mutation-pair effects from genotype-conditioned residuals that permit epistasis sign reversals.
How can replicated growth measurements distinguish genuine background-dependent epistasis sign reversals from noise in pathway-regularized residuals?
Requiring 95% credible intervals excluding zero in both backgrounds will yield ≥80% sign-reversal concordance across independent growth-assay batches.
Measure singles and pairs across eight backgrounds in independent batches; test whether 95%-credible reversals achieve ≥80% concordance.
Assay 120 mutation pairs and constituent singles across eight backgrounds in two batches; calculate 95%-credible reversal concordance.
Among 64 batch-one reversals with 95% credible intervals excluding zero, only 42 (66%) replicated in batch two.
Discovery-batch reversals with 99% credible intervals and ≥0.05 log-growth-unit effects in both backgrounds will replicate ≥80% across batches.
Reanalyze the 64 batch-one reversals using 99% credible intervals and ≥0.05 log-growth-unit effects in both backgrounds; assess batch-two concordance.
Of 30 batch-one reversals meeting both stricter criteria, 26 replicated in batch two (87% concordance).
Adopt reversal labels requiring 99% credible intervals and ≥0.05 log-growth-unit effects in both backgrounds; replication rose from 66% to 87%.
Reversal-QC v1 table records 64 candidates, background-specific effect estimates, 99% credible intervals, and batch-two outcomes for 30 qualifying calls.
Blindly audit Reversal-QC v1 by re-assaying singles and pairs for 30 qualifying and 34 rejected calls in batch three.
Batch-three assays reproduced 27/30 qualifying sign reversals versus 15/34 rejected calls, supporting reproducible background-conditioned interactions.
Which genetic-background representation enables pathway-regularized interactions to generalize to held-out backgrounds while preserving reproducible sign reversals?
Run leave-one-background-out validation comparing pathway-burden and raw-genotype embeddings against additive baselines on growth RMSE and Reversal-QC sign accuracy.
Pathway-burden RMSE was 0.096 versus raw-genotype 0.104 and additive 0.110 log-growth units; Reversal-QC sign accuracy was 83% (25/30).
Select pathway-burden embeddings: held-out RMSE fell 12.7% versus additive, with 83% Reversal-QC sign accuracy and 27/30 labels replicated.
Prospectively assay unseen pairs in new backgrounds; test pathway-burden for ≥10% additive-RMSE reduction and >75% independently measured sign-reversal accuracy.
Transfer pairwise epistasis between backgrounds matched by single-mutant growth-response profiles, using uncertainty-weighted neighbors to flag context-specific sign changes.
Does single-mutant response similarity identify transferable pair effects better than pathway-burden similarity without masking independently validated sign reversals?
Response-profile neighbors will beat pathway-burden RMSE (0.096 log-growth units) on held-out backgrounds while retaining >75% validated reversal accuracy.

Across leave-one-background-out folds, fit uncertainty-weighted background neighbors from single-mutant profiles; compare RMSE and batch-three-validated Reversal-QC v1 reversal accuracy against pathway-burden.
Response-profile neighbors achieved 0.091 versus pathway-burden’s 0.096 log-growth-unit RMSE; sign accuracy was 22/27 (81%) on batch-three-validated reversals.
Mask each test pair’s constituent singles before neighbor selection; recompute held-out-background RMSE and Reversal-QC v1 reversal accuracy against pathway-burden.
After masking constituent singles, neighbor RMSE rose to 0.103 versus pathway-burden’s 0.096; validated reversal accuracy fell to 19/27 (70%).
Pathway-burden-constrained neighbors using pair-masked single-mutant profiles will achieve held-out RMSE below 0.096 log-growth units and validated reversal accuracy above 75%.
Fit pathway-burden-constrained neighbors using pair-masked profiles; compare held-out RMSE and validated Reversal-QC v1 accuracy against 0.096 and 75%.
Pair-masked, pathway-constrained neighbors achieved 0.094 log-growth-unit held-out RMSE and 22/27 (81%) accuracy on batch-three-validated reversals.
Withhold nearest donor backgrounds; assess pair-masked constrained neighbors against 0.096 RMSE and 75% accuracy on validated Reversal-QC calls.
Without nearest donors, constrained-neighbor RMSE rose to 0.102 log-growth units and validated reversal accuracy dropped to 18/27 (67%).
Gate pair-masked neighbor transfer by cosine distance ≤0.20, otherwise use pathway-burden; predict RMSE <0.096 and validated reversal accuracy >75%.
Test ≤0.20 cosine-gated neighbors with pathway-burden fallback in standard and nearest-donor-withheld folds; measure RMSE and validated Reversal-QC accuracy.
Gated transfer achieved RMSE 0.093/0.095 log-growth units and validated reversal accuracy 22/27 (81%)/21/27 (78%) in standard/donor-withheld folds.
Adopt cosine-gated transfer with pathway-burden fallback: donor-withheld RMSE improved from 0.102 to 0.095 and reversal accuracy from 67% to 78%.
Prospectively assay 150 pairs in four new backgrounds; compare gated transfer against pathway-burden on RMSE and independently measured reversal accuracy.
Assay 150 pairs and singles across four new backgrounds; compare gated-transfer versus pathway-burden RMSE and independently replicated Reversal-QC reversal accuracy.
Prospective-150 v1 contains replicated pair and single growth measurements, both models’ predictions, and Reversal-QC calls across four new backgrounds.
Prospective-150: gated-transfer RMSE was 0.094 versus pathway-burden 0.101 and additive 0.109; independently replicated reversal accuracy was 29/36 (81%).
Select cosine-gated transfer with pathway-burden fallback: prospective RMSE improved 14% versus additive, with 81% independently replicated reversal accuracy.
Fit a transcriptome-conditioned mixture of shared and stress-state-specific epistasis experts to predict held-out growth and sign reversals.
Can pre-mutation transcriptomes identify background-specific epistasis without leaking growth responses from the mutation combinations being predicted?
Wild-type-only RNA-seq gating will achieve held-out-background RMSE below 0.094 log-growth units and >75% independently replicated reversal accuracy.
Sequence unmutated parents; train transcriptome-gated experts on eight backgrounds, then compare Prospective-150 RMSE and reversal accuracy against gated transfer.
Wild-type RNA-seq gating yielded Prospective-150 RMSE 0.097 versus gated transfer’s 0.094; reversal accuracy was 26/36 (72%).
Batch-correct wild-type RNA-seq with ComBat-seq, refit transcriptome-gated experts, and score Prospective-150 RMSE and independently replicated reversal accuracy.
ComBat-seq-corrected wild-type RNA-seq gating achieved Prospective-150 RMSE 0.092 log-growth units and independently replicated reversal accuracy 29/36 (81%).
Adopt ComBat-seq-corrected transcriptome gating: prospective RMSE improved from 0.097 to 0.092 and reversal accuracy from 72% to 81%.
Pre-register train-only ComBat-seq correction; collect parental RNA-seq before mutagenesis, then compare models on blinded combinations in four new backgrounds.
Assay 150 blinded pairs in four new backgrounds after parental RNA-seq; compare train-only-corrected gating with Prospective-150-calibrated transfer on RMSE/reversal accuracy.
Blind-150 v1 contains pre-mutagenesis parental RNA-seq, replicated growth measurements, frozen model predictions, and independently confirmed reversal labels.
On Blind-150, train-only-corrected gating achieved 0.090 versus transfer 0.096 and additive 0.108 log-growth-unit RMSE; reversal accuracy reached 31/38 (82%).
Using the frozen train-only-corrected gating model, shuffle Blind-150 parental RNA-seq across backgrounds, regenerate predictions, and compare RMSE and reversal accuracy.
Across 100 parental-RNA-seq shuffles, mean Blind-150 RMSE remained 0.090 and reversal accuracy 31/38, matching unshuffled gating.
Defer transcriptome gating despite 0.090 RMSE: parental-RNA shuffling preserves performance, so its added assay cannot justify deployment over transfer.
Replace new-background deployment with independent-culture parental RNA-seq and train-only normalization; require improvement over shuffled-RNA controls before restoring gating.
Resequence independently cultured Blind-150 parents; assess RNA-seq reproducibility and train-only-normalized gated RMSE and reversal accuracy against shuffled-RNA controls.
Blind-150 RNA-QC v2 contains independent-culture parental expression matrices, replicate correlations, train-only normalization parameters, and shuffled-control prediction scores.
With independent-culture RNA and train-only normalization, Blind-150 RMSE was 0.091 versus shuffled 0.098; reversal accuracy was 30/38 versus 25/38.
Reconsider transcriptome gating for prospective validation, not deployment: independent-culture RNA improved RMSE to 0.091 versus shuffled 0.098.
